title: Joining Speed Webb and the Vitaphone movie band
summary: The Willie Jones/Leonard Gay band joined Speed Webb; Roy Eldridge, Teddy Wilson and their brothers were in the band and Gus Wilson arranged.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And then, at the end of that, we joined Speed Webb's band. That band joined Speed Webb. That's how Speed Webb formed.

Yes. Because he had just came back from the Coast. He had a band out on the Coast, and he didn't bring it back East with him. I don't know... Maybe the guys wouldn't come with him. I really don't know. But I guess they all liked where they were. It was out in Los Angeles, and Los Angeles at that time was jumping, you know, and all kinds of work was out there -- movies and things. This was in the late Twenties.
And we joined his band. You know, he was the first band that had...the first Colored band that was in sound. They used to call it Vitaphone. Remember...?
Did I tell you about that?
Well, you mentioned a little bit about it.
Was that before you joined the band, that they did that movie stuff?
Yeah, that was before it. I was with Speed Webb... I mean, I was with Leonard Gay. In fact, the band wasn't called Leonard Gay's band, although Leonard was the
music director. The band was called Willie Jones' band. But Jones left, Willie Jones -- I don't know what happened to him.

Anyway, we got together, you know, with Speed, and Speed had very many promises, as they all do have. But nothing but promises. That's all. You dig? So we scuffled, and... Roy (Eldridge) was in the band and Teddy (Wilson) was in the band, and their brothers -- both had brothers, you know, and they were in the band.
Joe and Roy, and then Teddy and Gus. Gus played trombone, and he was a very great arranger. He was a good trombone player, too, but he was an excellent arranger.
